description: The bar chart, titled “QLoRA,” illustrates the computational cost, measured in FLOPs (floating-point operations), for six different fine-tuning methods applied to the Llama-3-8B model across ten NLP tasks, as described in the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “# FLOPs,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹⁸ to 10²⁰, with major gridlines at each power of ten. The horizontal axis lists the six methods: “Full FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “MTL-FT,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” each represented by a single vertical bar. The first five bars are colored orange, while the final bar, “Ours,” is distinctively colored green, visually emphasizing the proposed method. The bars are arranged in descending order of FLOP count: “Full FT” is the most computationally expensive, with a value slightly below 10²⁰; “TAG” and “LoRA” follow closely with values around 10¹⁹.⁵ and 10¹⁹.³ respectively; “MTL-FT” is next at approximately 10¹⁹.¹; “QLoRA” is lower at roughly 10¹⁸.⁷; and “Ours” is the least expensive, at approximately 10¹⁸.⁶. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that the proposed method (“Ours”) achieves performance comparable to the best baseline while requiring significantly fewer FLOPs — specifically, 45% less than the best-performing baseline, which appears to be “QLoRA” based on the relative bar heights and the context provided.
